headline: PM Tarique Rahman visits slain July protester's grave, gives family Tk 2mn
summary: The Prime Minister visited Md Wasim Akram's grave in Pekua and provided financial assistance to the family of the student killed during the July Uprising.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the grave of Md Wasim Akram, a slain July Uprising protester, in Pekua Upazila on Saturday afternoon. He offered prayers at the grave near Mehernama Bazar and met with Wasim's family, handing over a Tk 2 million savings certificate as financial aid.

Wasim was a fourth-year sociology student at Chittagong College and a member of Jatiotabadi Chhatra Dal. He was killed on July 16, 2024, during clashes between protesters, police, and Bangladesh Chhatra League activists in Chattogram’s Muradpur.
During the visit, the Prime Minister was accompanied by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and lawmaker Lutfur Rahman Kajol.

Separately, the Prime Minister formally launched a nationwide tree-planting programme at the Malumghat Reserved Forest in Dulahazara. He urged citizens to plant at least one sapling to ensure a healthier environment and cleaner air for future generations.
Tarique Rahman stated that the government aims to plant 50 million trees annually, with a goal of planting 250 million trees across the country over the next five years.
He also inaugurated the Patali Canal re-excavation project and toured the Dulahazara Safari Park with his wife, Zubaida Rahman, where he planted a nagalingam sapling.
Upon arriving at Cox's Bazar International Airport, the Prime Minister drove himself from the airport to Pekua, with Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed as his passenger.

headline: 648 children dead as measles outbreak kills 5 more in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports a surge in measles symptoms among children, with 84,899 cases since March 15.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), five children died from measles symptoms in the last 24 hours. Three of these deaths occurred in Dhaka, while one each was reported in Rajshahi and Mymensingh.
Since March 15, a total of 648 children have died due to measles symptoms. Of these, 92 deaths occurred after measles was officially confirmed.
The DGHS reports that 84,899 children have shown measles symptoms since March 15, with 69,606 of them being admitted to hospitals.
In the last 24 hours alone, 63 new cases of measles were confirmed, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 10,248.
Hospitalization rates remain high, with 672 children admitted in the last 24 hours. However, 577 children were discharged after recovering from the illness during the same period.
To date, 65,852 children have recovered and been discharged from hospitals since the start of the outbreak in March.
